title: Dallas BAPS Mandir Expects 12,000 for Diwali Annakut and Fireworks on November 10
excerpt: The Irving mandir's Diwali and Hindu New Year celebration on November 10 pairs the Annakut offering and a 'Light Beyond Lamps' exhibition with fireworks and a BAPS Charities food donation to Irving Cares.
body:
• The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Irving expects roughly 12,000 visitors for its Diwali and Hindu New Year celebration on Tuesday, November 10, from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.
  • The centrepiece is the Annakut, an offering of hundreds of vegetarian dishes prepared by devotees, alongside an exhibition titled "Light Beyond Lamps: Journey Through Hindu Sanskruti" and a closing fireworks and light-and-sound show.
  • BAPS Charities will make a food donation to Irving Cares as part of the event; its Dallas-area drive for the same nonprofit collected about 2,000 pounds of food in October 2025.
  • No ticket or registration details have been published for the BAPS event — Dallas-area readers should confirm entry arrangements on the mandir's page before travelling; the Radha Krishna Temple of Dallas in Allen runs its own Diwali programme November 5-10.

Dallas-Fort Worth's Diwali season peaks on Tuesday, November 10, when the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Irving hosts its Diwali and Hindu New Year celebration and expects roughly 12,000 visitors over the course of the day. The event runs from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m., two days after Diwali itself, which falls on Sunday, November 8 this year, Hoodline reported.

Annakut at the Centre

The afternoon is built around the Annakut, the traditional mountain of food offered to the deities for the Hindu New Year. BAPS describes the offering as hundreds of vegetarian dishes — snacks, sweets and savouries prepared by devotees and presented in gratitude — set against handcrafted Diwali decor. Visitors can also walk through an immersive exhibition, "Light Beyond Lamps: Journey Through Hindu Sanskruti," which explores Hindu values and traditions; Hoodline reported the same theme is being used across BAPS mandirs throughout North America for this year's Diwali and New Year celebrations.

The programme also weaves in the United States' 250th anniversary and a tribute to frontline heroes, with a dedicated stage segment and planned flag processions, before closing with a fireworks show and a light-and-sound experience.

Service Alongside Celebration

BAPS Charities, the organisation's humanitarian arm, will make a charitable food donation benefiting Irving Cares, a local nonprofit, as part of the event. The pairing has local history: a BAPS Charities food drive in the Dallas area from October 4 to 21, 2025, also for Irving Cares, collected about 2,000 pounds of food from volunteers of varied ages and backgrounds.

The Wider Dallas Diwali Week

The BAPS celebration caps a full week of Diwali programming across the metroplex. The Radha Krishna Temple of Dallas in Allen runs its Diwali Mahotsav from November 5 to 10, including the lighting of 11,111 diyas on Saturday, November 7, from 6:00 p.m., Lakshmi Puja on November 8 — the temple lists the Drik Panchang muhurat for Dallas as 5:52 to 7:46 p.m. CST — an Annakoot on November 9, cultural performances, a food festival and fireworks. A Frisco Diwali Mela is also scheduled for November 1 at Kaleidoscope Park, with dance, a talent stage, a kids' fun zone and vendors.

Planning Your Visit

Hoodline's report lists no ticket price, registration or RSVP requirement for the November 10 BAPS event, and the mandir's own page is the place to confirm entry and parking arrangements before setting out: see the BAPS Dallas mandir page. With 12,000 visitors expected across five hours, arriving early in the 3:00 p.m. window is the practical move for families who want the Annakut darshan and the exhibition before the evening fireworks crowd builds.
